description.to:
Outcome: Every tenant gets <site>.<platform domain> on day one (owner decision 3 recommends apyr.us, whose zone is in papyrus-production). One wildcard ACM certificate and one wildcard alias record point at the shared distribution; specific names already in use (p.apyr.us) keep their own distributions, which CloudFront allows. A reserved-names list (newsroom, www, api, mail, admin, our product names, existing tenant ids) is refused.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): the shared edge template (certificate, alias), Route 53 zone apyr.us, TenantDomain rows (PPY-31c45c), provisioning (PPY-70a429).

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/default-subdomain.feature):
Scenario: A new tenant is reachable at its subdomain
    Given tenant "harbour-news" is provisioned
    When "https://harbour-news.apyr.us/" is requested
    Then its starter site is served over HTTPS

Scenario: A reserved name is refused
    When a tenant asks for "newsroom"
    Then provisioning refuses it and suggests another

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-3bbbf9, PPY-31c45c. Blocks PPY-966722, PPY-70a429. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-fea16f.

Testing: Behave against staging with a staging wildcard domain.
Rollout: Shared stack; DNS change approved by Ryan.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: the wildcard shadows a future product subdomain. Mitigation: a specific record always wins; the reserved list is data.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
